title: trio-sdk-ergonomics-credential-handoff-and-stream-backpressure-hints-with-version-bumps
author: Aisha Patil
release_notes: Added credential handoff shim to improve multi-SDK session transitions; introduced stream backpressure hint header and ergonomic iterator improvements across Python/TS/Go SDKs; bumped SDK versions (Python, TypeScript, Go).
description: Motivation: teams integrating multi-language components often need seamless credential/session handoff when a caller in one language proxies or migrates a streaming session to another. This PR implements a light-weight credential handoff shim and a small set of stream-level backpressure hints so SDKs can coordinate without changing wire protocol compatibility. Goals: (1) Provide an explicit, opt-in handshake to attach a short-lived session lease to an existing stream so that downstream SDKs can continue a session with minimal reauth; (2) Surface ergonomic async/iterable improvements so Python and TypeScript idioms feel natural; (3) Improve Go context cancellation and connection pooling around long-lived streaming; (4) Bump SDK package versions to signal minor API surface additions. Work completed: single continuous change that touches SDK adapters, protocol glue, tests, and docs; no protocol breaking changes to server APIs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked and reviewed (ENG-1427) - [x] End-to-end integration test in ci-matrix - [x] Backwards-compatibility validation against existing hosted API - [x] Updated SDK CHANGELOGs and migration notes - [x] Demo app updated to show cross-language session handoff Notes on compatibility: the handoff is opt-in and carried as an expiring token blob in an extra header (X-Redwood-Session-Lease). When absent, behavior is unchanged. Streaming backpressure hints are advisory (X-Redwood-Stream-Hint: prefer-slow-client) and are intentionally soft so servers can ignore them. Security: leases are short lived, signed by issuing control plane, and validated server-side. For Private installs we rely on existing KMS/HSM signing integrations. This PR bundles small ergonomic API surface changes: Python async generator has a new resume_with_lease(lease_token) helper; TypeScript iterator exposes resumeWithLease(leaseToken) and a small ergonomic cancelReason argument; Go SDK adds StreamResume(lease string, ctx context.Context) and derives child contexts on handoff to ensure cancellation semantics are preserved. Version bumps: python -> 1.23.0, typescript -> 3.2.0, go -> 1.1.0. See release_notes for details.
